results.title: Legitimate comparison text ("<10:00", ">8:30/mi", "HR <140 bpm", ...) typed into cardio fields through the UI is saved exactly as typed
Round trip: a cardio entry containing < and > exports, previews, restores into a clean profile and is byte-identical
Every LEGIT string passes backup validation as a cardio value, in every cardio field
HTML-like cardio text is refused when logging, with a message explaining that < and > are allowed as comparison signs, and nothing is stored
Malicious cardio text in a backup file is refused at preview: restore is never offered, the reason names the cardio entry and field, and storage is untouched
Stored markup that predates this fix is never executed or turned into elements: the cardio "PREVIOUS" line shows it as literal text
Data keys in a cardio record must be plain identifiers: markup, control characters, __proto__ and over-long keys are refused on import
Cardio values must be text or numbers: nested objects, arrays, booleans and non-finite numbers are refused; data must be an object
Control characters and over-long text in cardio values are still refused
Import protection elsewhere is NOT weakened: < or > is still refused in work-set, stretch, strength and activator history and in record ids/names/machine fields
Historical cardio records (old shapes without id or sessionId, numeric-looking text, empty values, unknown keys) still import and round-trip byte-identically
Existing cardio records are never altered: loading, rendering, exporting and a refused import leave pa_cardio_hist byte-identical
A draft with a typed-but-unsaved cardio value containing < resumes with it after reload, and survives backup/restore
Every place that renders cardio history is escaped: static check that no cardio value reaches innerHTML unescaped
Unfinished markup with no closing ">" is plain text: accepted, stored as typed and rendered literally and inertly
A full real workflow with cardio containing < and > still passes every other backup property: draft, finished session, history all restore identically
